nom: SKIN1004 Madagascar Centella Probio-Cica Bakuchiol Eye Cream

segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin, sensitive eye areas, or a reactive skin barrier report the cream is calming and non-stinging, with no irritation even when the barrier is compromised.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin describe the cream as strongly hydrating, easing crepey or dry under-eye skin especially in cold weather.
segments.combination: A reviewer with dry-to-combination skin reports the cream hydrates well and works as a smooth makeup base.
segments.mature: Reviewers over 40 or using the product for aging concerns say the effect on wrinkles and dark circles is mild and note they wouldn't expect dramatic results from an eye cream at this stage.

concerns.aging: Most reviewers see little to no change in fine lines or wrinkles in the short term, describing effects as mild, subtle, or requiring more time; a minority report visible tightening, smoothing, or smaller-looking wrinkles, and one long-time retinol user found bakuchiol gentler and non-drying on the eyes.
concerns.dehydration: Reviewers consistently describe the cream as hydrating, with under-eyes feeling smoother, plumper, and less dry, including relief from crepey skin in cold weather; absorption is fast without greasiness.
concerns.redness: One reviewer with a compromised skin barrier reports the product does not sting even when their skin is reactive that day.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer notes the formula supports the skin barrier and does not sting during barrier flare-ups; no other barrier-specific complaints appear.
concerns.spots: No reviewer specifically discusses spots or hyperpigmentation as a distinct concern; a few mention brightening or reduced discoloration under the eyes.
concerns.blemishes: One reviewer switching from retinol reports no milia or irritation-related bumps, and another notes heavier eye creams usually cause bumps under her eyes but this one does not.
concerns.oiliness: Multiple reviewers state the cream is not greasy or oily despite being moisturizing, including those with oil-sensitive under-eye skin.

extraits.titre: No good for dark under circles
extraits.texte: I received this product in exchange for my honest review. I've been testing this for about 2-3 weeks and all I can say is my under eye area is maybe a little more hydrated than before. Unfortunately it's made no difference for my dark circles or my fine lines thus far. The product itself easily absorbs and the applicator is fun and easy to use.

extraits.titre: Wonderful for skin, but cannot be worn under makeup
extraits.texte: I love what this cream does for my eyes, it brightens and soothes and is very sensitive skin friendly. But I got this as my day eye cream because it doesn't have retinol, and every time I try to put it on make up it pills up, rolls up, leaves peely layers, and I have to remove the makeup and the eye cream and put on something else so that I can wear makeup. I've tried different concealers and foundations and it does the same thing always.

I received this as a free sample in exchange for a review. Madagascar Centella Probio Cica Bakuchiol Eye Cream has been a solid addition to my routine. I love that it comes in a tube so I don't have to dip my fingers into a pot. The texture feels moisturizing without leaving any greasy residue and it sits nicely under makeup without pilling. I haven't noticed a dramatic change in fine lines but at 40 I don't expect any eye cream to work miracles. I can't speak to how it performs on dark circles since that's not a concern for me but overall it's a dependable gentle formula that keeps the area smooth and comfortable.

Texture-wise, this is what really stood out to me: creamy but lightweight, in such a way that it doesn't feel greasy/heavy under the eyes. It absorbs pretty quickly and works well under sunscreen and concealer-zip pilling here. I love that it doesn't sting one bit, even on days when my skin barrier is acting up. It's also very light and refreshing. Result-wise, I didn't see dramatic wrinkle removal, but my under-eye area looks smoother and a bit brighter. The biggest difference was the dryness-my fine lines look softer because the area stays hydrated longer throughout the day. The bakuchiol seems gentle; I've reacted to retinol eye products before, but this didn't cause irritation or milia. It's more of a maintenance eye cream than an anti-aging one. If you have deep wrinkles/eyebags, you probably won't see huge changes. It works better as a preventive or soothing barrier-support eye cream rather than a corrective treatment. All in all, it feels like more of a daily eye cream for sensitive skin than a miracle worker — and I actually like that about it. I'd recomend it especially if retinol eye creams are too much for you but you want something that will improve the texture over time. It makes me feel super refreshed as a part of my skincare routine.

I don't use many eye creams because I feel like they don't do much for me and are kinda gimmicky. That being said, I really enjoyed the Madagascar Centella eye cream. It feels super refreshing under my eyes and has become part of my eye routine. I've noticed that my normal eye discoloration seems slightly reduced and my eyes, that are very dry, don't feel as bad in the morning after using this.

I recently tried this eye cream from skin1004 and it works good! I do have dry to combination skin and this really hydrates my undereyes. This works as a base when I apply my makeup and makes my undereyes look so smooth. After using it for a while I noticed, my undereyes look more bright and hydrated!
I really like this eye cream. My under eyes got crepey with the cold weather. This eye cream did the trick. My under eyes are nice and smooth after a few uses.
